subject: business-studies
title: Break-even Foundations Adventure
welcome_lead: You'll meet fixed and variable costs, contribution per unit, and the break-even idea.
meta_desc: GCSE Business Studies break-even foundations — fixed and variable costs, contribution per unit.
final_note: You can define contribution and find the break-even point of a simple business.

concepts.def: Output level where total revenue = total cost
Cost not affected by output (rent, salaries)
Selling price minus variable cost per unit

walkthroughs.body_html:
Break-even tells a firm how many units it must sell to cover all costs.

Below it: loss. Above it: profit. Right on it: zero profit/loss.

Contribution per unit = selling price − variable cost per unit.

It's what each sale 'contributes' towards paying off the fixed costs.

Break-even quantity = fixed costs ÷ contribution per unit.

Example: fixed £6,000, price £10, VC £4. Contribution £6. Break-even = 6000 ÷ 6 = 1,000 units.

mcqs.q: Break-even is where total revenue equals.

numericals.q: Fixed costs £4,000. Price £10. Variable cost £6. What is the break-even output, in units?

free_texts.q: What's the term for 'selling price minus variable cost per unit'? One word.
